stories.new_fact: AP reported that in-person voting for the midterms begins Friday in Virginia and that voters in Idaho, Minnesota and South Dakota can cast absentee ballots in person.
stories.new_takeaway: Election-administration disputes now become live voter-instruction and county-workflow problems, not only court-calendar issues.
stories.why_now: Friday, September 18 is the first day of in-person voting in Virginia and the start of the final six-week operating window before November 3.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent episodes covered the mail-ballot injunctions and DHS voter-check project; this segment uses the new event that voting has begun and shifts the takeaway from litigation to execution.
stories.uncertainty: Federal efforts around voter data and noncitizen searches continue, and misinformation can still alter voter behavior even without a rule change.
stories.watch: Watch county-level voter instructions, early-vote processing and any evidence that federal election-administration efforts create voter confusion.

stories.new_fact: Columbus leaders introduced legislation requiring Columbus Water and Power to establish peak rates or other fees and charges for large load/high-volume users, including data centers, with a September 28 agenda date.
stories.new_takeaway: The local policy question is whether data-center growth pays for the infrastructure capacity it requires rather than shifting costs to residents and small businesses.
stories.why_now: Axios reported the package September 17 after a Wednesday press conference and the ordinance is on the September 28 council agenda.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent local stories covered Moritz downtown, school report cards, Hilliard parkland and housing approvals; this is a different utility-rate and infrastructure-cost story.
stories.uncertainty: The ordinance sets an expectation and deadline but does not itself rewrite rates; Columbus Water and Power must still design a concrete structure.
stories.watch: Watch the September 28 council vote and the rate design Columbus Water and Power brings back.

stories.new_fact: Freddie Mac reported the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage averaged 6.95% as of September 17, up from 6.76% the prior week, while the 15-year averaged 6.26%.
stories.new_takeaway: The public weekly benchmark has caught up to near-seven-percent pricing, forcing purchase-file requalification and updated concession, lock and buydown math.
stories.why_now: The PMMS update was published September 17, within 24 hours of the episode cutoff.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent home-lending coverage discussed daily pricing, application triage, preapproval refreshes and MI termination; this segment uses the fresh weekly benchmark and keeps the Fed as context.
stories.uncertainty: Post-Fed long-yield relief may or may not pass through to daily mortgage pricing; the weekly survey lags some desk moves.
stories.watch: Watch whether the 10-year Treasury and MBS pricing let daily quotes move below Freddie's 6.95% weekly average.
stories.workflow: Active purchase-file requalification, lock counseling, seller-credit negotiation, buydown math and approval-letter refreshes.

stories.new_fact: Business Insider reported that JPMorgan is pairing a $2,000 monthly Claude spending limit for some users with Devspace, a containerized AWS-hosted environment that restricts Claude's access to credentials and internal systems.
stories.new_takeaway: The banking-AI control question shifts from whether coding assistants are useful to whether they can run with identity, logging and no standing entitlements to sensitive systems.
stories.why_now: The report was published September 18 and changes a previously tracked JPMorganChase AI productivity row.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent AI-in-banking segments covered Zopa, Goldman, Schwab, Pockit, Rogo, FIS and Truist; JPMorgan was in the ledger but had not been used as a current control-architecture story.
stories.uncertainty: No measured code-quality, defect, security-finding or developer-productivity outcome was disclosed; it is unclear whether or when all Claude-using engineers will move into Devspace.
stories.watch: Watch for measured coding-assistant outcomes or a wider JPMorganChase rollout of the sandboxed architecture.
stories.ledger_row_changed: JPMorganChase | lane 7 | status remains production but row updated with Claude Devspace containment controls, $2,000 limit for some users, about 8,000 Claude licenses and about 1,900 Devspace Teams members; evidence rank reputable reporting; no outcome metric disclosed.

stories.new_fact: AP reported that Claude is leading 26% of Anthropic's model R&D, participates in about 90% of R&D in collaboration with humans, and that about 30,000 agents were doing research and engineering work as of August.
stories.new_takeaway: Frontier labs are starting to disclose metrics for AI-led AI development, but the same disclosure shows why outsider-comparable methodology and agent oversight matter.
stories.why_now: AP published the Anthropic disclosure September 18, and the metric is a new frontier safety and capability measurement.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent frontier sections covered OpenAI misalignment reporting, embedded evaluators, China model competition, GPT-Rosalind and misuse reporting; this advances the self-improvement measurement thread with a different takeaway.
stories.uncertainty: Anthropic says the model is not fully autonomous and AP reports it is unclear how close the company believes it is to recursive self-improvement.
stories.watch: Watch whether other frontier labs publish comparable AI-R&D contribution metrics and whether third-party evaluators can verify them.
stories.frontier_bar: Agent and tool-use advances plus safety measurement; measured by Anthropic and reported by AP, not independently replicated.

stories.new_fact: AP reported the S&P 500 rose 1.1%, the Dow gained 0.6%, the Nasdaq rose 1.7%, Brent crude fell 1% and the 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.93% on Thursday.
stories.new_takeaway: The first post-hike relief signal helped stocks and long yields, but mortgage affordability still needs pass-through into rate sheets.
stories.why_now: The market move occurred September 17 after the September 16 Fed hike.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent market segments previewed Fed-day and oil pressure; this uses the first post-decision session and stays compact.
stories.uncertainty: One session does not establish a sustained trend, and Freddie's weekly mortgage survey still rose sharply.
stories.watch: Watch whether the 10-year yield stays below 5% and whether MBS pricing improves enough for lenders to reprice.

stories.new_fact: Forecast sources indicated a warm Friday with highs in the low to mid 80s and weekend thunderstorm chances.
stories.new_takeaway: Columbus listeners should use Friday for errands or outdoor work where possible and recheck radar before weekend activities.
stories.why_now: Weather affects same-day and weekend planning.
stories.previous_coverage: Routine weather appears daily; this is current practical planning only.
stories.uncertainty: Scattered storms can change timing by neighborhood.
stories.watch: Recheck local radar before Friday evening and weekend outdoor plans.
